This one’s for you — the hearts that believed in us, stood by us, and helped Sarposh become what it is today. Every smile, every word of encouragement, every visit — we are here because of you

Gratitude fills our hearts as we look back on this journey — a journey made possible by you. From our very first day to today, Sarposh has grown not just as a restaurant, but as a community, a feeling, a home away from home.

To everyone who walked through our doors, shared a meal, told a friend, or simply sent us love from afar — this reel is a small thank you to each of you. Your support, your warmth, and your belief in our story have meant the world to us.

Sarposh is more than food — it’s people, it’s memories, it’s you. We’re deeply grateful for every kind word, every celebration, every challenge that shaped us. Thank you for being a part of our family. Here’s to continuing this journey together.🧡

#WithGratitude  #SarposhFamily #JourneyOfLove #Gratitude #ThankYouFromSarposh #SarposhFamily

Community meal at Sarposh

The food community in Bangalore came together this weekend to support one of our finest restaurants in an afternoon that truly celebrated what makes this one of India’s greatest cities.

@sarposhfoods has won awards as Bangalore’s best restaurant. One of India’s greatest food writers Marryam Reshii has said that it is the best Kashmiri food you can eat in any restaurant anywhere. It was started a little over five years ago as a way for the founder @azmatalimir to share her Kashmir heritage with the city of Bangalore. It wasn’t just about the authentic food but craft, community, culture.. a bridge through which we could discover a bit of Kashmir.

Sadly, after the terrible terrorist attacks in Pahalgam, Azmat and Sarposh were the victims of ugly online abuse and a campaign to boycott, bringing the business to its knees. 

I personally found this shocking because you can’t attack all Kashmiris because of the evil actions of a terrorist group. And you can attack innocent individuals because of actions they have nothing to do with. I don’t claim to be political but this isn’t about politics. It’s basic humanity to support innocent people who are being targeted. 

Bangalore is a city that has always been welcoming, inclusive and tolerant, a true melting pot. So to celebrate the true spirit of Bangalore, fifty food lovers gathered at Sarposh this Sunday for a wazwan feast. 

And my god what a feast it was. Nice different lamb dishes, each one distinct and unique and full of flavour. We started with the extraordinary Tabak Maaz and Sheekh kebab, and moved on to a soft, perfectly beaten rista and Rogan josh. The tartness of the plums in the alau Bukhara korma was followed by my favourite Kashmiri dish, the aab gosht. This is a dish you almost never get in restaurants, that you can’t really take away and repack because of the need to get the milk at the right time and temperature and this was just perfection. A fragrant, spicy marchewangan kormeh was next and finally a goshtaba to end the meal. 

All this was accompanied by a gucchi pulao…

“My (football) association has been banned by the Jammu and Kashmir Football Association (JKFA). My players, clubs and I myself cannot coach anyone. I am banned as a human being. I have no alternative but to leave Kashmir,” said Marcos.
In 2010, Marcos sent two Kashmiris to Brazil for higher training. Subsequently, a second group of six Kashmiris went to Brazil and got official coaching degrees from the Brazilian sports ministry and the Sao Paulo Football Federation.
He was beaten up by security forces at the height of Amarnath Land Row agitation in 2008 but the matter was later resolved amicably.
He was asked to leave the country as the Union Home Ministry had refused to extend his stay in the valley.
